Furthermore, the company severely lags behind its peers in capital efficiency, generating a low return on assets of 0.95% against a sector benchmark of 1.49% and a weak return on equity of 1.53% compared to the 4.11% sector benchmark [E7, E8]. To compound these fundamental weaknesses for investors, the stock offers a nonexistent dividend yield of 0.00% [E3]. The bull relies on past share price growth and sector tailwinds, but these figures completely disconnect from Samor Reality’s actual operational reality of a -1383% compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E13].
